body:
Can you share a reproducer?

> Am 04.04.2015 um 20:07 schrieb huguesb notifications@github.com:
> 
> We recently noticed that one of our Netty services was intermittently ignoring requests, causing the caller to timeout. Adding LoggingHandlers all over the place revealed that the failing request was received but never made it out of HttpRequestDecoder.
> 
> The connection is reused by the client and saw multiple similar requests before the server somehow choked on the last one. The server uses autoRead=false in case that is relevant.
> 
> We promptly reverted to 4.1.0-Beta3 and this failure mode completely disappeared. A quick look at the commit log between the two tags show a significant refactor of HttpRequestDecoder and some more subtle changes to ByteToMessageDecoder which are probably responsible for the regression.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

I wish I could but extracting a small reproducer from our codebase would take a lot of work and that's not a worthwhile time investment at this point since 4.1.0-Beta3 works for us.

However if you can provide a diff to add extra verbose logging I'd be happy to run the full reproducer with that and report the results here.

@normanmaurer I went ahead and added the logging myself and I zeroed in on the issue.
1. The channel is set to autoRead=false.
2. upstream handler calls read()
3. a fragmented HTTP request is received (in this case the packet is fragmented before the last \n separating headers and content).
4. HttpObjectDecoder doesn't fire any channelRead because decoding isn't complete
5. HttpObjectDecoder fires channelReadComplete but
   - invokedNextChannelRead is false because no channelRead was fired hence the channelReadComplete is not propagated up the pipeline
   - invokedPrevRead is **always false** because read() is propagated on the _outbound_ context and HttpObjectDecoder is on the _inbound_ context hence read() is not propagated down the pipeline
6. STALL

Possible fixes I can think of:
- make ByteToMessageDecoder a duplex handler to ensure invokePrevRead is set correctly
- in ByteToMessageEncoder.channelReadComplete() when autoRead is false and no channelRead() was fired, call read() instead of firing channelReadComplete()
- always propagate channelReadComplete() upstream for non-duplex handlers when autoRead is false

I'm not very familiar with the 4.1 branch so I'll refrain from submitting a PR until someone more knowledgeable picks the best solution.

The more I think about it the more convinced I become that the correct solution would be to move read() to ChannelInboundHandler and propagate it down the _inbound_ context (as opposed to down the _outbound_ context as is currently the case)

Similarly I think it would make more sense for channelWritabilityChanged() to be moved to ChannelOutboundHandler and propagated up the _outbound_ context.

Rationale: read() modulates channelRead() and channelWritabilityChanged() similarly modulates write()
so it makes sense for each of these pairs to be in the same interface.

However it's probably too drastic an API change to be integrated in 4.1 at this time. Maybe 5.0 then?

issue.title: EmbeddedChannel and autoRead=false

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
While working on a fix for #3529 and #3587 I discovered that the behavior of EmbeddedChannel doesn't accurately reflect that of a real channel when autoRead is false.

The fix I came up with breaks DefaultChannelPipelineTest.testChannelReadNotTriggeredWhenLast and upon reading, the test code looks wrong, in the sense that the expected behavior is not consistent with what I would expect from a real channel with autoRead=false

Again, it all comes back to `invokePrevRead` which would have been true for the original handler but isn't  for the handlers added after the channel is created, hence read() is not called and `channelRead1.get()` returns `1` instead of the expected `3`

issue.title: Fix handling of non-auto read for ByteToMessageDecoder and SslHandler

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Motivation:

Our automatically handling of non-auto-read failed because it not detected the need of calling read again by itself if nothing was decoded. Beside this handling of non-auto-read never worked for SslHandler as it always triggered a read even if it decoded a message and auto-read was false.

This fixes [#3529] and [#3587].

Modifications:
- Implement handling of calling read when nothing was decoded (with non-auto-read) to ByteToMessageDecoder again
- Correctly respect non-auto-read by SslHandler

Result:

No more stales and correctly respecting of non-auto-read by SslHandler.
